chapters.summary: Through the prophet Haggai, God calls the governor of Judah and the people to stop tending only to their own houses while the temple lies neglected, and promises to bless them if they rebuild it.
keyPoints: The people say the time to rebuild the house of the LORD has not yet come, but God points out that they live in paneled houses while his house lies in ruins.
God calls the people to consider their ways - they have sown much but harvested little, and eat and drink without ever being satisfied.
The people obey the voice of the LORD and fear him, and God promises, "I am with you."
chapters.application: Let us examine the priorities of our own lives - are we putting God's work first? When we seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, he will surely provide all we need and give us a satisfaction nothing else can match.

chapters.summary: God encourages the people to rebuild the temple, promises to bless them, and declares that he will shake all nations, bringing peace and glory to his house.
keyPoints: God promises to be with the people - do not fear, but be strong and get to work.
The treasures of all nations will be brought in, and the latter glory of this house will be greater than the former.
God will pour out blessing on the people - from this day on, they will be blessed.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, God promises to be with us. As we devote ourselves to his work, he will surely bless us and fill our lives with his glory.
